mechaber.1#main: Signs of pure domestic animal and wild animal. In it are 3 seifim: The signs of domestic animal and wild animal were explained in the Torah, and they are two signs: chewing the cud and split hooves; and every domestic animal and wild animal that has no teeth in the upper jaw and no "nivin" — which are knobs of flesh like protruding teeth in children — and some say nivin are two teeth above, one from here and one from here at the ends of the jaws (explanation: "and strike him on the cheek" — Targum: on her jaw). It is known that it is pure, and this is recognizing a young camel that has no nivin until it grows. And everything that chews the cud splits the hoof except camel, hare, and hyrax which chew the cud and do not split the hoof — one need not be concerned they have teeth above or nivin; therefore one who finds an animal in the desert and does not recognize it and its hooves are cut off — for he cannot check them — should check if it has no teeth and no nivin above; it is known it is pure, and this is recognizing a young camel. And everything that splits the hoof chews the cud except pig; therefore if one found an animal whose mouth is cut off — for he cannot check it — he should check its legs if its hooves are split; it is known it is pure, and this is recognizing a pig. If it has horns it is removed from doubt of pig and is pure. And no impure animal's flesh under its elbow joint goes back and forth to whichever side one cuts it except the wild ass (explanation: wild donkey); therefore one who finds an animal whose mouth and hooves are cut off — for he cannot check them — should check the flesh under the wing of the elbow joint after slaughtering if it goes back and forth — it is pure, and this is recognizing a wild ass. (Human flesh is forbidden to eat from the Torah) (Ran chapter Acharai Mot and Rambam 22 Laws of Forbidden Foods law 3 and so Korban Aharon Shemini daf 64a unlike apparent meaning in Tosafot Acharai Mot and Rosh that human flesh is not forbidden from Torah — and so Bach).
mechaber.2#main: An impure animal that gave birth to the form of a pure species — even though it has all signs of purity — is forbidden; and a pure animal that gave birth to the form of an impure species is permitted even though it has all signs of impurity; and specifically if it gave birth before us; but if one left it pregnant and afterward found an impure species following it, even though it is wrapped after it and nurses it — forbidden, lest it was born from the impure one and wrapped after the pure one.
mechaber.3#main: One born of a treifah is permitted.

siftei-kohen.1#א: ["Signs of domestic animal and wild animal were explained in the Torah. Meaning: the signs between pure and impure domestic animal and wild animal were explained in the Torah as explained and proceeds; but signs between wild animal and domestic animal were not explained in the Torah — rather the Sages gave signs as below beginning siman 80; investigate:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ב: ["And some say nivin are, etc. — this language appears primary, and so appears Maharshal's view chapter These Treifot siman 101 — see there:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ג: ["Forbidden to eat from the Torah. Explanation: by positive commandment but not by negative commandment — so explained there; and here it deals with flesh separated from a live person; but flesh of the dead is forbidden even for benefit by Torah law for all — as below siman 79:"]
siftei-kohen.2#א: ["Impure that gave birth, etc., and pure that gave birth, etc. — the reason is explained in the mishnah: everything from the impure is impure and from the pure is pure; and this rule applies only to what is forbidden by negative commandment, not to what is forbidden only by positive commandment — therefore human milk is permitted though his flesh is forbidden — as below siman 81 seif 7; so Rav HaMagid and Korban Aharon there:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ב: ["And pure that gave birth to impure form is permitted. It appears specifically like impure domestic animal; but if it gave birth like pure bird — forbidden — as Taz wrote above siman 13 seif 5 that one who slaughters an animal and finds likeness of pure bird — forbidden to eat; one should not distinguish found inside versus born — for Gemara chapter HaMakish (daf 61b) implies born is worse — there even for R' Shimon who forbids only when it entered the world, in its mother's belly permitted — see there; and so Tosafot there (daf 69a) s.v. Alma — and in Asheri there explicitly likeness of bird forbidden also when born — see there; and the reason: because it is not fulfilled:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ג: ["And afterward found impure species. Even if no impure one in its herd we are concerned perhaps it came from another herd — Torah doubt to be stringent — so Rav HaMagid laws of forbidden foods and Maharshal and Acharonim agreed:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ד: ["Even though wrapped after it, etc. Taz wrote: and it appears to me the same for impure left pregnant and we did not see it give birth and we see pure form wrapped after it — we are also stringent lest this one was born from it and forbidden — end of his words; and it is simple and proven explicitly in Gemara chapter 3 of Bechorot (daf 24a) — see there; and see siman 16 s.k. 5 and siman 316 seif 2:"]
siftei-kohen.3#_: One born of treifah. Explanation: it became pregnant before it became treifah — otherwise treifah does not give birth; or it deals with definite treifah — as above siman 57 seif 8 and below chapter 6 seif 9; and even though generally we hold fetus is thigh of its mother — why here we hold CM siman 409 cow that damaged collects from offspring for treifot — different since matter depends on animal's vitality — we hold treifah is not alive and this fetus is alive — Tosafot Acharai Mot daf 58a s.v. vehalachta and Rashba in his novellae and Tur and even though treifah egg we hold siman 86 forbidden — different there since it grew in prohibition — so in Gemara Acharai Mot; and Taz wrote Maharar Piovish z"l: requires further study if mother was trampled while pregnant whether trampling harms also the offspring — end of his words.

turei-zahav.1#א: That has no nivin until it grows. For since it has no teeth above it chews the cud — and so in Tur.
turei-zahav.1#ב: Under the elbow joint. Explanation: bone of the elbow that they call anka.
turei-zahav.1#ג: Human flesh, etc. — this is Rambam's view chapter 2 Laws of Forbidden Foods; and Rosh wrote chapter Acharai Mot it is forbidden only rabbinically, and if separated it is permitted; and it is wondrous why Tur and Beit Yosef did not bring this dispute.
turei-zahav.2#_: Even though wrapped after it. Some challenge from siman 316 where nursing helps for firstborn exemption — Derishah answered well: there exempt because certainly it gave birth some offspring from compassion and nursing — unlike here; and Levush: same for impure left pregnant unseen birth — if we see pure wrapped after impure we are stringent lest this was born from it — forbidden; Derishah brought Beit Yosef: saw pig wrapped after ewe — firstborn exempt but forbidden to eat.
turei-zahav.3#_: One born of treifah permitted. Beit Yosef in name of Rashba: though they said fetus is thigh of its mother — they also said treifah is not alive; since mother's prohibition is only because it is not alive and this fetus is alive and its life does not depend on mother's life — permitted, end of his words. And what Maharar Piovish wrote: requires further study if mother trampled while pregnant whether trampling harms offspring — end of his words.

baer-heitev.1#א: In the Torah. Meaning signs between pure and impure were in Torah; signs between wild animal and domestic animal — Sages gave signs as below siman 80.
baer-heitev.1#ב: Nivin. Shach wrote this language appears primary and so Maharshal.
baer-heitev.1#ג: Until it grows. For since no teeth above it chews the cud.
baer-heitev.1#ד: Human. Shach: only positive commandment not negative; only flesh separated while alive; dead flesh forbidden even benefit — all agree — below siman 79; Taz: Rosh holds human flesh only rabbinically — see there; wonder Tur and Beit Yosef did not bring this view.
baer-heitev.2#א: Forbidden. Reason in mishnah: from impure impure, from pure pure; rule only for negative commandment prohibition — therefore human milk permitted though flesh forbidden — siman 81 seif 7; specifically gave birth like impure domestic animal; like pure bird forbidden — siman 13.
baer-heitev.2#ב: Wrapped. Taz: and I say same impure left pregnant unseen — see pure wrapped after — stringent; Levush same; if saw pure wrapped after impure — forbidden lest born from impure.
baer-heitev.3#_: Treifah. Shach: deals pregnant before treifah — otherwise treifah does not bear; or definite treifah — siman 57 seif 8; though generally fetus is thigh of mother — CM 409 cow damages collects offspring for treifot — different — depends on vitality — treifah not alive, fetus alive — Gemara Acharai Mot; Taz Maharar Piovish: if mother trampled while pregnant whether harms offspring — requires further study.

beer-hagolah.1#ב: Baraita there and as Gemara explains there.
beer-hagolah.1#ג: Tur as second explanation in Rashi; and so in Tur HaChadash.
beer-hagolah.1#ד: As first explanation in Rashi there; and so; and Tosafot wrote this language is primary.
beer-hagolah.1#ו: Tur and so Rashba; and so.
beer-hagolah.1#ז: Also statement of Rav Chisda there.
beer-hagolah.2#ב: Statement of R' Yochanan there daf 24.
beer-hagolah.3#_: From implication of Gemara Beitzah daf 6 and Rav in Chullin daf 75; and even though we say fetus is thigh of its mother — since mother's prohibition is only because it is not alive and this fetus is alive and its life does not depend on mother's life.

beur-hagra.1#א: Signs of domestic animal and wild animal, etc. Mishnah and Gemara — their name "wild animal" is included, etc., and there 71a.
beur-hagra.1#ב: And some say, etc. Avodat HaTaharah; and they brought proof from what is written chapter 6 of Shabbat they remove its nivin and chapter 2 of Bava Kamma he removed its nivin, etc.
beur-hagra.1#ג: If it has horns, etc. Rashi in Niddah 61b s.v. veyesh — there is none like it without cloven hooves except pig as written in Torah; and what mishnah says "and there are" refers to impure — nevertheless not distinguished by horns alone since mishnah there is R' Dosa as Tosafot in name of Rivam Chullin s.v. elu hen and Avodat Yom Tov siman 80; and so Ran and all commentators like Rivam, not like Rabbenu Tam there.
beur-hagra.1#ד: Human flesh, etc. — for it is written "this you shall eat" and no other; and it counted only animal species — "and it was." Rambam relied on Torat Kohanim Shemini chapter 4 — and human flesh, etc., implies negative commandment only; and though he also said milk because of flesh — and proof: first he said hoofed walkers impure are impure implying pure completely — here changed and said not negative commandment; thus resolved Gemara Acharai Mot 60a counts blood and milk not flesh; Torat Kohanim answered flesh and milk from two teachings; Gemara only one teaching; and from Torat Kohanim and end of Keritot we derive blood from bird and animal but not that blood and milk derive even from issur and from bird and animal we only hear not warned on blood negative commandment — but from issur of what comes from impure we do not derive; therefore Acharai Mot learns both from one verse; Torat Kohanim learns on flesh that is not negative commandment — Ran. (Lekut) Human flesh, etc. — from what is written beginning chapter Dam Shechitah to exclude blood of walkers, etc.; also no question since entirely permitted; but Rashba wrote siman 79 permitted from Torah — only mitzvah of separation; proof from Dam Shechitah — rejected because gid forbidden in him prohibition of gid depends on palm of hand — and question Chullin 92b on animal but not bird, etc.; but everything in him and his species certainly forbidden — main case was human — see there at length (end).
beur-hagra.3#_: One born, etc. — as Sages in Temurah 21a and Chullin 58a; and so sugya chapter 1 Beitzah and Chullin 75a one who slaughters treifah, etc. (Lekut) One born, etc. — as R' Yehoshua in Temurah and Chullin 58a; and so sugya there 78a-b and chapter 1 Beitzah 6a and Avodat HaTaharah and Tosafot Bava Kamma 47a s.v. mati, etc., and Sanhedrin chapter 2 s.v. fetus, etc., and Chullin there s.v. vehalachta, etc., and we learn from this (end).

kereti.1#א: Were explained — to recognize impure from pure; but to recognize wild animal from domestic animal for milk and covering not from Torah — only from tradition of Sages.
kereti.1#ב: If it has horns — from this proven impure animal has horns except pig — see Peleti perhaps grooved horns, etc., siman 80 — see there; but plain horn is not a sign.
kereti.1#ג: And pure, etc. — if it gave birth like bird form — forbidden — Shach and Peri Chadash.
kereti.2#א: Found impure species — even if no impure in herd — nevertheless forbidden — Torah doubt — concerned perhaps came from elsewhere.
kereti.2#ב: Even though wrapped, etc. — and same impure left pregnant unseen birth — unless signs of purity and impure wrapped after — we say stringently forbidden lest this one wrapped after — all stringencies whether or not and other matters — not to be lenient.
kereti.3#א: One born of treifah — does not exist that treifah gives birth; Shach wrote deals definite treifah — we do not say definite treifah if it gave birth nevertheless treifah — but in reality does not exist — only pregnant then treifah — see siman 56 Kereti and Peleti at length.
kereti.3#ב: Permitted — for treifot we do not say fetus is thigh of mother — treifot depend on weakness of body — animal body was healthy — offspring healthy; however Taz wrote Maharar Piovish: if mother trampled while pregnant whether trampling harms offspring; if alive b'nei chorin permitted like other doubt of trampling; Peri Chadash: if trampled opposite offspring concerned poison reached offspring; if trampled above toward neck poison does not reach offspring — no doubt permitted; see Peleti question from chapter HaTaruvot — see there.

kaf-hachayim.1#_: (1) [Seif 1] Signs of domestic animal and wild animal were explained in Torah, etc. — meaning signs between pure and impure in Torah as explained; signs between wild animal and domestic animal not in Torah — Sages gave signs as below siman 80 — Shach s.k. 1. Shaarei De'ah 1.
kaf-hachayim.2#_: (2) There. And every domestic animal without teeth in upper jaw, etc. — specifically no teeth in upper jaw; but bumps it has above and below — as known.
kaf-hachayim.3#_: (3) There. And its hooves split — separated above and below with two nails; some hooves split above but not fully separated below connected — Rashi in Chumash Shemini. Kenesset HaGedolah Hagahat Tur 4, Leket HaPardes 1, Beit Yosef 1, Shulchan Gavoah 1, Shaarei De'ah 1, Beit Yitzchak 1, Arukh HaShulchan 3, Zivchei Tzedek 1.

peleti.1#_: And if it has horns — removed from pig doubt — proves horns alone are not a sign — it is pure since split hooves and doubt only on pig which has horns as proof — Rivam Chullin 59 s.v. elu explains Gemara: these are signs of wild animal to permit its milk — must return to check hooves; if has hooves must return to horns; R' Dosa holds horns alone sign for wild animal — impure have no horns; Niddah "everything with horns has hooves" — R' Dosa; Ran agrees; stam mishnah R' Dosa — halachah like R' Dosa since stam mishnah — Peri Chadash: halachah like stam mishnah; from this arose question Maharam of Rekesh on Ran Rosh Hashanah shofar of impure animal invalid for mitzvah — how exist — all with horns have hooves; they did not err plainly; Shulchan Aruch here requires both horns and hooves — only there Ran holds halachah R' Dosa — question Ran contradicts himself. But if halachah R' Dosa nevertheless Gemara chapter 1 teaches all with horns is sign for wild animal — grooved split horns; R' Dosa on "everything with horns has hooves" — grooved horns; two meanings horns — do not distance dispute — plainly even R' Dosa impure wild animals have no horns but impure domestic may have grooved horns — wild animal certainly; if has grooved horns and hooves certainly wild animal; Niddah mishnah R' Dosa — grooved horns; Rambam explains mishnah: horns to distinguish wild from domestic for milk — Maharsha; if so no question — halachah stam mishnah grooved only; but other domestic impure may have horns; Ran forbids shofar for mitzvah — clear; Tosafot Yom Tov Niddah. For practical halachah most poskim including Rambam like first Tanna and Rif did not cite R' Dosa or Niddah mishnah — halachah first Tanna; though halachah stam mishnah — Chullin stam domestic and wild animal said from Torah — did not also say horns sign — like Beitzah fish asks spine visible — therefore first Tanna; horns not sign at all only for milk not whether pure — mishnah deals with that. But from Shabbat question — tachash in Moses' days had one horn on forehead like primordial ox — Tosafot Chullin 59b s.v. vekares — Shabbat follows R' Dosa — horns sign for pure domestic animal — especially one horn — all the more impure may have two horns; hard say entire Gemara not halachah — Peri Chadash also — do not say horns grooved — still question from tachash; say in sharpness: certainly halachah only two horns per R' Dosa — not one horn — otherwise what proof from tachash; must say rule only for tachash known pure with one horn for milk; not in count of pure species — Gemara wanted prove all agree pure — for first Tanna simple; for R' Dosa say only temporary and does not break Moses' rule all with horns have hooves — tachash impure had horns — rule false — say temporary — does not break rule transmitted; if only one horn does not break rule as above; tachash pure not counted — Gemara proves all agree pure — why not decide beast or wild animal — if impure species could have one horn; if pure no known domestic with one horn — certainly wild animal; also primordial ox and unicorn have one horn — did not decide; all answered in sharpness. Plainly most poskim agree majority with horns are pure; minority also impure have horns — do not rely on sign alone — like lung checks — do not rely majority kosher — if doubt before us do not rely majority since happened — all the more cut hooves — forbid; but majority with horns are kosher — when live animal testified horns — presume majority separate — has signs; if check certainly has signs; if debate permit or forbid distant testimony horns — presumption majority separate has signs. Peri Chadash: if horns alone treifah — Shach: if outer salted not remained inner not salted — forced ein hana'asur — fire absorbs more — reversed comparison not forced; outer fire expels from inner; coated goose salted — permitted; do not innovate dispute without proof — investigate.
peleti.3#_: One born of treifah, etc. Taz wrote Maharar Piovish: if mother trampled pregnant whether harms offspring — Peleti and Peri Chadash require further study; Gemara chapter HaTaruvot treifah cow — establish mother trampled — fetus treifah from drisah doubt unrecognized — mixes easily. I say those Rishonim hold fetus treifah — mishnah do not offer to Most High but to layman suffices as Rashi — not Tosafot — no question we redeem for inspection not feed dogs; Tosafot establishments fall drisah of wolf puncture — has inspection — redeem not feed dogs; if establish treifah mother trampled — fetus treifah no remedy — how teach graze — do not redeem kodshim to feed dogs — see siman 57 and my ways to resolve.

pitchei-teshuva.1#_: Human flesh. See Peri Chadash and responsum Yad Eliyahu siman 45 and responsum Rashbash siman 518 — elaborated — see there.
pitchei-teshuva.2#_: Forbidden. See responsum Yad Eliyahu siman 2 — doubted if law like truly impure or we say since signs of purity — forbidden only to eat — ramifications if slaughter removes nevelah, milk if truly impure no karet even if permitted to trade, limb from live animal customs — many ramifications — inclined not called impure except for eating not other matters — lenient and stringent; Torah doubt do not be lenient — has stringencies of pure and impure — see there; see below siman 271 s.k. 2.
pitchei-teshuva.3#_: From treifah. (Avodat HaTaharah: and what requires further study if mother trampled — see above siman 57 s.k. 3 from this).

yad-avraham.1#_: (Siman 79 seif 1 in hagahah) Human flesh forbidden from Torah. See Bayit Chadash what he wrote incident: infant fell in honey vat and died — Tov Ayin forbade honey because human flesh forbidden from Torah; in my opinion no prohibition for poskim who permit after not separated and does not enter honey only taste; but forbid other reason — died there — flesh of dead forbidden benefit from Torah — we derive from ever min hachai; Mishnah chapter 2 Avodah Zarah ever min hachai forbids in any amount — so dead forbids any amount — his words not compelled — ever min hachai forbids in amount because counted item; here only if actually mixed not mere taste.
yad-avraham.2#_: (There seif 3) One born of treifah permitted — when pregnant then treifah; but treifah then pregnant — if occurs as Rambam wrote — offspring forbidden.
